output:
# Tidewater Dispatch — H2 2026 Roadmap

**Assumptions:** 5-day engineer-weeks (per Jane). 24 eng-weeks/quarter is already net of on-call and maintenance. Confidence used as a decimal. No item is split across quarters.

---

## 1. Scored backlog

**Formulas**

- **Effort (norm.)** = effort in engineer-weeks. All items were submitted in weeks except F7, which was submitted in engineer-days: 45 days ÷ 5 days/week = **9 eng-weeks**. (Read as weeks, F7 would score 6.7 and never be considered — the sheet needs a units column.)
- **RICE** = Reach × Impact × (Confidence ÷ 100) ÷ Effort (norm.)

| ID | Item | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort (as submitted) | Effort norm. (eng-wks) | RICE | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F6 | Invoice PDF redesign | 600 | 0.5 | 90% | 3 wks | 3 | **90.0** | 1 |
| F1 | Offline mode (technician app) | 420 | 2 | 80% | 16 wks | 16 | **42.0** | 2 |
| F7 | Technician skills matching | 250 | 2 | 60% | 45 days | 9 | **33.3** | 3 |
| F4 | Customer self-booking portal | 510 | 1 | 70% | 12 wks | 12 | **29.8** | 4 |
| F2 | Route optimisation v2 | 300 | 3 | 50% | 20 wks | 20 | **22.5** | 5 |
| F3 | SAML single sign-on | 35 | 1 | 100% | 6 wks | 6 | **5.8** | Committed |
| F5 | Map provider migration | — | — | — | 8 wks | 8 | n/a | Mandatory |

**Separate categories**

- **F5 – Mandatory (unscorable).** No reach/impact/confidence because it is cost-avoidance, not customer value: miss 31 Dec and we either pay +40% on the map contract or lose maps for all 640 accounts. Forcing a score would be theatre (reach 640 × impact 3 × 100% ÷ 8 ≈ 240 would "win" trivially). Handled as a fixed deduction from H2 capacity with a hard deadline, scheduled before any discretionary item.
- **F3 – Committed (scored, but not ranked by score).** RICE is low because reach is one customer, but it is contractual ($180k ARR, exit clause at 31 Oct). Scheduled on deadline, not score.

Discretionary capacity after F3 + F5: 48 − 14 = **34 eng-weeks**.

---

## 2. H2 plan

| Quarter | ID | Item | Effort (eng-wks) | Sequencing / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Q3 (Jul–Sep)** | F3 | SAML SSO | 6 | Start 1 July, target live mid-Sept → ~6 weeks slack before 31 Oct clause |
| | F1 | Offline mode | 16 | Starts in parallel; 2 spare weeks act as buffer for F1's 80% confidence |
| | | **Q3 used / available** | **22 / 24** | 2 spare |
| **Q4 (Oct–Dec)** | F5 | Map provider migration | 8 | Start 1 Oct, done by end Oct → ~2 months slack before contract end |
| | F4 | Self-booking portal | 12 | Starts early Oct alongside F5 |
| | F6 | Invoice PDF redesign | 3 | Filler; first to drop if F5 slips |
| | | **Q4 used / available** | **23 / 24** | 1 spare |
| **H2 total** | | | **45 / 48** | 3 spare; no item split across quarters |

**Why this packing:** F3 and F5 together in Q3 (14 wks) leaves 10 wks, into which only F6 fits — wasting 7 weeks and pushing F1 to Q4. Putting F3 in Q3 and F5 first-thing in Q4 keeps both deadlines comfortably covered and fills 45 of 48 weeks. F5 sits at the front of Q4 deliberately so that any Q4 disruption (holidays, incidents) hits F6/F4, not the contract deadline.

---

## 3. Cut list

| ID | Item | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| F2 | Route optimisation v2 (20 wks) | Doesn't fit with F1: 16 + 20 = 36 > 34 discretionary weeks, and F1 has double the RICE (42 vs 22.5) at higher confidence. Also blocked on F5, which can't land before October, so F2 couldn't start before Q4, where F5 + F2 = 28 > 24. First unblocked candidate for Q1 2027. |
| F7 | Technician skills matching (9 wks) | Lost the final slot to F4 by a narrow margin: F7 has a slightly higher RICE (33 vs 30) but F4 delivers more absolute value (510×1×0.7 = 357 vs 300), fills Q4 better (23/24 vs 20/24 used), and F7's estimate is a single, unvalidated day-based figure at 60% confidence. Swap-in candidate if F4 discovery kills it or its scope shrinks to ≤9 weeks. |

---

## 4. Memo

**To:** Richard Roe, Mary Major
**From:** Senior PM, Tidewater Dispatch
**Re:** H2 2026 roadmap

Mary — SSO ships in Q3, sequenced first, targeting mid-September. That leaves roughly six weeks of slack before Brightwell's 31 October clause, and it isn't competing with anything else for capacity.

Richard — Route Optimisation v2 is not in H2, and I want to be straight about why. After the two non-negotiables (SSO and the map migration, which we must do or pay +40% / lose maps), the squad has 34 engineer-weeks for features. Offline mode needs 16; Route v2 needs 20. They don't both fit, so this was one or the other. Offline mode is the top request in churn interviews, reaches 420 accounts, and scores twice as high (RICE 42 vs 22.5) at 80% vs 50% confidence. Route v2 also depends on the map migration, which can't finish before October — so it physically couldn't start before Q4 and wouldn't fit there either. Doing the migration this year makes Route v2 the first unblocked item for Q1 2027.

What would change my mind: (1) named, qualified enterprise deals that close *only* with Route v2 and whose ARR exceeds what's at churn risk without offline mode; (2) a two-week spike that lifts confidence toward 80% and the estimate below ~14 weeks; or (3) funded extra capacity (e.g., a contractor on the map migration) freeing 8 weeks. Any one of those and I'll reopen it before the Q4 lock on 15 September.

Also shipping in H2: the self-booking portal (510 accounts) and the invoice PDF redesign. Skills matching is held for 2027.
